title: Bluetooth speaker experiment (14 subjects, 6 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG recordings from 14 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball BCI task for controlling a Bluetooth speaker, one of several home appliances in the original study. Participants viewed flashing stimuli for six classes on an LCD display while 31-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz. Each participant completed 50 training and 30 testing blocks, with online visual feedback in the testing blocks. The data support research on ERP-based BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning for home appliance control.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG was recorded with an actiCHamp amplifier (Brain Products) using active electrodes in a standard 10-20 montage. Sampling rate was 500 Hz and the reference was linked mastoids. A visual oddball paradigm with a 750 ms stimulus onset asynchrony was used, with Target and NonTarget events. Each subject completed one session of 50 training and 30 testing blocks in a laboratory.
